timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: We can just add security after we build it, right?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: That's archaeology, not architecture. Fixing flaws after a breach is the expensive way.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What does security by design actually mean?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Thinking about security at the beginning, so the software is secure from the outset.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So it's about the design phase?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. Threat modeling, secure defaults, least privilege — all decided before code.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Because the structure decides how the system behaves. Flaws in the foundation are everywhere.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What's the difference from secure coding?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Secure coding is how you write. Security by design is how you architect before writing.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: They give the design rules: least privilege, fail secure, defense in depth.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So security becomes a property of the design?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Not an add-on. An architectural property.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Dramatically. A design fix costs hours. A breach costs everything.
